claims.promise: A collector can find one coin by year and denomination in seconds, correct a wrong field in place, and remove a coin he sold or gave away in a single tap, so the catalogue follows the collection instead of drifting behind it.

evidence.finding: On com.miccron.coinoscope, 3.7 stars over 1M+ installs, a 1-star review of 18 sampled reads "Super hard to use. You can't search for a specific dated coin. To edit out a pic from my collection (if i sell or gift one) has proven elusive".

claims.deferredReason: No UI exists yet: search, in-place editing and deletion over the coin record are the first screens to build and the first fixture set to write.

claims.promise: The catalogue is a file the collector owns: it needs no account, no subscription and no network, and it moves in and out as CSV, so the record survives losing the phone and never depends on a service staying alive.

evidence.finding: 4 of the 13 critical reviews read in the coin pocket are classified paywall, 31 percent of that critical set, and all three largest coin apps measured declare in-app purchases while the 500K+ catalogue leader declares none.

claims.deferredReason: The CSV round-trip and the local-store-without-network guarantee are unbuilt; the promise is resolved only when both have tests that fail against a network or account dependency.

claims.promise: The app records what a collector actually records, country, denomination, year, mint mark, grade, what was paid, what it is valued at and where it is stored, instead of being a photo identifier that cannot be corrected or trusted.

evidence.finding: About 15 of 30 visible results on the coin collection shelf are photo identifiers with in-app purchases, while about 12 of 30 are catalogues, and the 50K+ identifier com.colnect.identify.coin sits at 2.6 stars with an entry complaint quoted in the proposal.

claims.deferredReason: The record schema is defined in the proposal but not in code; it is resolved when the editor covers the full field set and a fixture proves every field round-trips through CSV.

claims.promise: It is bought once and never advertises: there is no subscription, no trial, no upsell after the unlock and no advertising identifier collected.

evidence.finding: 2 of the 13 critical reviews in the pocket are classified ads, and the installed catalogue leader com.spencerpages declares neither advertising nor in-app purchases.

claims.deferredReason: The billing capability and the single unlock sheet are not built; the ads half is resolved by shipping with no advertising dependency at all.

claims.promise: Coin photos come from the system photo picker, so the app requests no camera and no storage permission and its install prompt asks for nothing.

evidence.finding: The Play compliance floor in AGENTS.md states the Photo Picker is preferred and that permissions must be minimized; no permission is declared in this recipe's plan.

claims.deferredReason: The photo picker is not wired up and the manifest has not been authored, so the zero-permission claim cannot yet be checked against a built APK.

claims.promise: Several collections can be kept side by side, each with its own count and total, so a bullion stack and a graded set are never averaged into one meaningless number.

evidence.finding: The measured shelf splits between bullion and graded collecting, and the catalogue apps in it expose a single undifferentiated list rather than per-collection totals.

claims.deferredReason: The collection model is a design decision recorded in the proposal, not code; it is resolved when per-collection totals render and a fixture proves two collections do not share a total.
